title: Late-diastolic pulse-area modulation does not establish an incremental respiratory-rate benefit in two public cohorts
abstract: Adding late-diastolic pulse-area fraction to five conventional PPG respiratory-modulation spectra did not establish a transferable improvement in respiratory-rate estimation. Equal-record MAE changed from 4.554 to 4.720 breaths/min in BIDMC and from 2.890 to 2.780 in independent CapnoBase. Baseline-minus-augmented gains were -0.167 [-0.367, 0.013] and 0.110 [-0.174, 0.437], respectively (95% paired-record bootstrap intervals). Both intervals include zero; this exploratory negative implementation result is not evidence that diastolic morphology lacks respiratory information.
